mappings.rationale: Requires a senior-management-approved information security policy that is periodically reviewed, which is exactly 5.1's policy approval and review cycle, plus 5.4's requirement that management drive security application.

Quantified risk assessment with prioritization and periodic refresh is an ISO 27001 clause 6.1.2 management-system requirement; no ISO 27002:2022 control describes performing risk assessments, so forcing it onto a policy or compliance clause would be a false map.

Risk treatment decisions (accept/mitigate/transfer/avoid) against risk appetite is ISO 27001 clause 6.1.3; ISO 27002:2022 lists treatment options as controls but has no clause for the treatment decision process itself.
Names authorized representatives with the technical skill and authority to coordinate security enterprise-wide, which is 5.2's definition and allocation of security roles with competence.
Two distinct obligations: clearly defined and allocated security responsibilities (5.2) and mandatory signed non-disclosure agreements for those holding them (6.6).
Maintaining procedures for contacting regulators and law enforcement on security matters is the literal subject of 5.5 Contact with Authorities.
Maintaining contacts with security forums and professional associations for threat and best-practice awareness is the literal subject of 5.6.
Periodic independent review of security policies, procedures and their implementation for adequacy and effectiveness is 5.35 verbatim in substance.
Developing the policy document with defined objectives and scope is 5.1; the explicit requirement that it align to legal, regulatory and contractual compliance obligations is 5.31.
Review of the policy at planned intervals and on significant change is the review provision written into 5.1 itself.

Assigns policy administration to a named information security officer (5.2 role allocation) whose duty is ensuring organization-wide adherence to the policy (5.36 compliance with policies and standards).
Identifying and mitigating risks arising from business processes that involve third parties is the core of 5.19 Information Security in Supplier Relationships.
Requires security requirements be established and agreed in formal contracts with any third party that accesses, processes or stores information, which is 5.20's agreement content requirement.
Service level agreements defining security requirements and deliverables are the documented supplier-agreement terms covered by 5.20.
Regular monitoring, review and audit of third-party service delivery against agreed terms is 5.22 verbatim in substance.
Maintaining an inventory of information assets to enable their identification and recovery is 5.9 Inventory of Information and Other Associated Assets.
Classification guidelines governing handling (5.12) and the explicitly required labeling of classified assets (5.13).
Documented and periodically reviewed acceptable use rules for information assets binding all personnel is 5.10 Acceptable Use of Information.
Policies defining user security roles and responsibilities so personnel understand their obligations is 5.2 Information Security Roles and Responsibilities.
Background verification of employment candidates, weighted to sensitive and critical-system roles, is 6.1 Screening.
Employment contracts that reference the security policy and state the employee's security obligations is 6.2 Terms and Conditions of Employment.
Management must brief users on their security roles before access is granted, which is 5.4's duty on management to require personnel to apply security per policy.
Regular awareness updates plus role-appropriate training for all employees is 6.3 Information Security Awareness, Education and Training.
A formal disciplinary procedure for employees who commit a security breach is 6.4 Disciplinary Process.
Defining and assigning responsibilities for termination or change of employment is 6.5 Responsibilities After Termination or Change of Employment.
Employees and third-party users must return all organizational assets on termination, which is 5.11 Return of Assets.
Removal on termination and adjustment on role change of access rights is the provisioning/revocation lifecycle in 5.18 Access Rights.

Defining and implementing security perimeters around areas holding information processing facilities is 7.1 Physical Security Perimeters, despite this control sitting in the Operations Security domain.
Correct maintenance of equipment to preserve availability and integrity is 7.13 Equipment Maintenance; the mandated annual maintenance agreement is a local addition ISO does not quantify.
Operating procedures for information processing facilities documented, maintained and made available to users is 5.37 Documented Operating Procedures.
Segregating conflicting duties and areas of responsibility to reduce unauthorized modification or misuse is 5.3 Segregation of Duties.
Formal control of changes to processing facilities and systems that affect information security is 8.32 Change Management.
Separation of development, test and operational environments to prevent unauthorized change to production is 8.31 verbatim in substance.
Monitoring, tuning and projecting resource use to meet future performance needs is 8.6 Capacity Management.
A policy on the use of cryptographic controls to protect information is the first half of 8.24 Use of Cryptography.
Policy on the use, protection and lifetime of cryptographic keys across their full lifecycle is the key-management half of 8.24; ISO 27002:2022 has no separate key management clause.
Security perimeters protecting areas containing sensitive or critical information processing facilities is 7.1 Physical Security Perimeters.
Entry controls on secure areas so only authorized personnel gain access is 7.2 Physical Entry.
Designing and applying physical security to offices, rooms and facilities by asset sensitivity is 7.3 Securing Offices, Rooms and Facilities.
Physical protection against natural disasters, malicious attack and accidents is 7.5 Protecting Against Physical and Environmental Threats.
Physical protection and working guidelines for personnel inside secure areas is 7.6 Working in Secure Areas.
Controlling and isolating delivery, loading and other unauthorized-entry points from processing facilities is the loading-area provision inside 7.2 Physical Entry.
Protecting equipment from power failure and other supporting-utility disruptions (power, water, telecoms) is 7.11 Supporting Utilities.
Protecting power and telecommunications cabling from interception, interference and damage is 7.12 Cabling Security.
An access control policy established, documented and reviewed against business and security requirements is 5.15 Access Control.
Formal user registration and de-registration is 5.16 Identity Management; the resulting assignment of access rights to authorized users is 5.18.
Account creation, modification and deactivation is 5.16 Identity Management, and the authentication half of the requirement is 5.17 Authentication Information.
Interactive password management systems enforcing password quality rules are the password provisions of 5.17, implemented through 8.5's secure authentication mechanisms.
Terminating inactive sessions after a set period and restricting connection times for high-risk applications are explicit session-control provisions of 8.5 Secure Authentication.

Securing electronic messaging is the electronic-messaging transfer rule in 5.14; the internet-use half corresponds to 8.23 Web Filtering, so the control spans two clauses rather than matching either fully.

Authentication and anti-fraud controls for online transactions are the transaction-integrity requirements of 8.26, and the explicit dual-control requirement for transaction authorization is 5.3 Segregation of Duties.

Protecting e-commerce information crossing public networks from fraud, dispute and unauthorized modification is the public-transaction protection requirement inside 8.26 Application Security Requirements.
A formal authorization process for allocating and revoking access rights to information systems is 5.18 Access Rights.
Lifecycle handling of electronic and printed media is 7.10 Storage Media, and the explicit secure disposal requirement is 7.14.
Restricting and tightly controlling utility programs capable of overriding system and application controls is 8.18 Use of Privileged Utility Programs.
Clear desk policy for papers and removable media plus clear screen policy for processing facilities is 7.7 verbatim in substance.
Reporting information security events through management channels as quickly as possible is 6.8 Information Security Event Reporting.
Requiring employees and contractors to note and report observed or suspected security weaknesses is the weakness-reporting half of 6.8.
Establishing management responsibilities and incident procedures in advance is 5.24 Incident Management Planning and Preparation; the quick orderly response those procedures deliver is 5.26.
Quantifying and monitoring incident types, volumes and costs to drive improvement is 5.27 Learning From Information Security Incidents.
Collecting, retaining and presenting incident evidence in conformance with legal requirements for follow-up legal action is 5.28 Collection of Evidence.
Specifying security control requirements in the business requirements for new or enhanced information systems is 8.26 Application Security Requirements.

Controls built into applications to ensure correct processing and prevent corruption map to 8.26's input, processing and output validation requirements; ISO 27002:2022 dropped the standalone correct-processing controls, so the fit is partial.
Procedures controlling software installation on operational systems to block unauthorized or untested deployment is 8.19 Installation of Software on Operational Systems.
Producing, retaining and reviewing audit logs of user activity, exceptions, faults and security events is 8.15 Logging; the one-year retention floor is a CBSL-specific addition.
Procedures for monitoring use of processing facilities to detect unauthorized activity is 8.16 Monitoring Activities.
Managing and controlling networks to protect systems and applications using them is 8.20 Networks Security.
Identifying security features, service levels and management requirements of network services and writing them into network service agreements is 8.21 verbatim in substance.
Establishing rules for software and system development with security across the lifecycle is 8.25, and the coding-practice component of those rules is 8.28 Secure Coding.
Careful selection, protection and control of test data against unauthorized access or corruption is 8.33 Test Information.
Measures preventing intentional or unintentional information leakage through unauthorized disclosure is 8.12 Data Leakage Prevention.
Supervising and monitoring outsourced software development with licensing and compliance terms is 8.30 Outsourced Development.
Timely acquisition of technical vulnerability information, exposure evaluation and remediation is 8.8 Management of Technical Vulnerabilities word for word in substance.

A near-duplicate restatement of 13.12 emphasizing hardware and software control measures, so it lands on 8.8 for remediation and 8.9 for the hardening/configuration side, but adds nothing distinct to either.

Establishing and getting senior approval for an enterprise-wide business continuity framework is the planning obligation of 5.29 Information Security During Disruption, though 5.29 addresses maintaining security in disruption rather than the BCP governance framework itself.
Business impact analysis and continuity risk assessment is the BIA-driven basis 5.30 requires for ICT continuity, feeding the disruption planning of 5.29.
A process to keep information security requirements satisfied during disruption and recovery is precisely 5.29 Information Security During Disruption.
Creating and maintaining continuity plans for critical operations is 5.29's plan requirement, with the ICT recovery capability those plans depend on covered by 5.30.
Routine testing, maintenance and revision of continuity plans is the exercise-and-test provision of 5.30 ICT Readiness for Business Continuity, keeping 5.29's arrangements verified.
